definition: A heart rate faster than expected for the clinical context.
plain: The heart is beating faster than expected.
example: The handover note records tachycardia, describing rate rather than the underlying cause.
note: Rate thresholds depend on age and context; the term alone does not identify a cause.

definition: A heart rate slower than expected for the clinical context.
plain: The heart is beating more slowly than expected.
example: Bradycardia is documented as an observation in the clinical record.

definition: Inflammation of the pericardium, the sac around the heart.
plain: The protective sac around the heart is inflamed.
example: The letter uses pericarditis to name the affected tissue precisely.
note: The literal parts suggest “inflammation around the heart”; the specific structure is the pericardium.

definition: Inflammation of the heart muscle.
plain: The muscular tissue of the heart is inflamed.
example: Myocarditis and pericarditis refer to different anatomical structures.

definition: Inflammation of the inner lining of the heart, often involving the valves.
plain: The inner surface of the heart is inflamed.
example: The referral differentiates endocarditis from myocarditis.

definition: A procedure that widens a narrowed or obstructed blood vessel.
plain: A narrowed blood vessel is opened wider.
example: The procedure list includes coronary angioplasty.
note: The word parts mean vessel repair; clinical use often refers to balloon-based widening.

definition: A recording of the electrical activity of the heart.
plain: A tracing of the heart’s electrical signals.
example: The electrocardiogram is the resulting record, not the recording instrument.

definition: Persistently raised arterial blood pressure.
plain: Blood pressure remains above the expected range.
example: Hypertension appears in the patient’s recorded medical history.
note: This is a meaning-focused split; diagnosis requires appropriate measurements and clinical criteria.

definition: A disease in which plaque builds up within arterial walls.
plain: Plaque accumulates in the walls of arteries.
example: The report describes atherosclerosis of the coronary arteries.
note: Atherosclerosis is a specific form of arteriosclerosis, not a synonym for every type of arterial hardening.

definition: The subjective experience of difficult or uncomfortable breathing.
plain: A person feels short of breath.
example: The patient reports dyspnoea on exertion.
note: Dyspnoea is a symptom; it is different from an objectively increased breathing rate.

definition: An increased breathing rate for the relevant age and context.
plain: Breathing is faster than expected.
example: Tachypnoea describes the observed respiratory rate.

definition: A temporary cessation of breathing.
plain: Breathing stops for a period.
example: Apnoea is recorded as an event, rather than as a description of breathlessness.

definition: A lower-than-expected oxygen level in arterial blood.
plain: There is too little oxygen in the arterial blood.

parts.meaning: below or deficient (a form of hypo-)

example: The record distinguishes hypoxaemia from tissue hypoxia.
note: Hypoxaemia refers to blood; hypoxia refers to tissues.

definition: Insufficient oxygen availability at the tissue level.
plain: Body tissues do not receive or use enough oxygen.

parts.meaning: below or deficient (a form of hypo-)

example: The teaching discussion compares hypoxia with hypoxaemia.

definition: Visual examination of the airways using a bronchoscope.
plain: A clinician looks inside the airways with a specialised scope.
example: Bronchoscopy appears in the investigation section of the note.

definition: Inflammation of the bronchial airways.
plain: The larger airways in the lungs are inflamed.
example: The suffix in bronchitis describes inflammation, not a specific organism.

definition: Air within the pleural space.
plain: Air collects between the lung and the chest wall.
example: The imaging report describes a pneumothorax.
note: The precise location is the pleural space; “air in the chest” is only the literal clue.

definition: Inflammation of the stomach lining.
plain: The lining inside the stomach is inflamed.
example: Gastritis names the tissue process, not the cause.

definition: Inflammation involving the stomach and intestines.
plain: The stomach and intestines are inflamed.
example: The word gastroenteritis contains two roots.

definition: Endoscopic examination of the upper digestive tract, including the stomach.
plain: A flexible scope is used to look inside the upper digestive tract.
example: Gastroscopy is listed under procedures, rather than symptoms.

definition: Enlargement of the liver.
plain: The liver is larger than expected.
example: The examination note records hepatomegaly.

definition: Surgical removal of the gallbladder.
plain: An operation to remove the gallbladder.
example: A previous cholecystectomy is documented in the surgical history.

definition: Difficulty swallowing.
plain: Swallowing is difficult.
example: The referral uses dysphagia to describe a swallowing symptom.
note: Do not confuse dysphagia (swallowing) with dysphasia (language impairment).

definition: Pain along the distribution of a nerve.
plain: Pain follows a nerve pathway.
example: The note uses neuralgia to describe the type and distribution of pain.

definition: Disease or dysfunction of one or more nerves.
plain: One or more nerves are damaged or not working normally.
example: The phrase peripheral neuropathy specifies the part of the nervous system involved.

definition: Inflammation of brain tissue.
plain: The brain itself is inflamed.
example: Encephalitis is distinguished from inflammation of the meninges.

definition: Paralysis affecting one side of the body.
plain: One side of the body is paralysed.
example: The rehabilitation note documents right hemiplegia.
note: Hemiparesis means weakness on one side, rather than paralysis.

definition: An acquired impairment of language expression or comprehension.
plain: A person has difficulty using or understanding language.
example: The note describes aphasia as a language impairment.
note: Aphasia does not necessarily mean a complete absence of language; clinical meaning is broader than the literal word parts.

definition: Pain in a joint.
plain: A joint hurts.
example: Arthralgia describes pain without itself establishing joint inflammation.

definition: Inflammation of a joint or joints.
plain: One or more joints are inflamed.
example: Arthritis and arthralgia describe different concepts.

definition: A joint disorder involving cartilage changes and other joint tissues.
plain: A joint condition affecting cartilage and surrounding joint structures.
example: The problem list includes osteoarthritis.
note: Its clinical meaning is more specific than the literal “bone and joint inflammation.”

definition: Pain in a muscle or muscles.
plain: Muscles feel painful.
example: Myalgia is a symptom term.

definition: Infection and inflammation involving bone and bone marrow.
plain: An infection affects the bone and its marrow.
example: The clinical context gives myel its bone-marrow meaning in osteomyelitis.
note: Myel/o may mean bone marrow or spinal cord; context selects the meaning.

definition: Reduced bone strength associated with low bone mass and structural deterioration.
plain: Bones become more fragile.
example: Osteoporosis is recorded as a bone condition, not joint inflammation.

definition: Inflammation of the skin.
plain: The skin is inflamed.
example: Dermatitis describes a skin process; further wording may specify its cause.

definition: Situated or administered beneath the skin.
plain: Under the skin.
example: The note describes a subcutaneous nodule.

definition: Removal of cells or tissue for examination.
plain: A small cell or tissue sample is taken and examined.
example: A skin biopsy is listed as a diagnostic procedure.
note: The literal parts do not fully convey the modern clinical meaning.

definition: Redness of the skin.
plain: An area of skin appears red.
example: The examination describes local erythema.
note: A descriptive sign rather than a diagnosis; appearance varies with skin tone.

definition: A red blood cell.
plain: A blood cell that carries oxygen using haemoglobin.
example: The full blood count includes measurements relating to erythrocytes.

definition: A white blood cell.
plain: A blood cell involved in immune defence.
example: Leucocyte is the singular form; leucocytes is plural.

definition: A reduced platelet count in the blood.
plain: There are fewer platelets than expected.
example: The laboratory comment uses thrombocytopenia for a low platelet count.
note: Thrombocytes are platelets; the term is not a deficiency of blood clots themselves.

definition: A haemoglobin concentration below the appropriate reference range.
plain: The blood has less haemoglobin than expected.
example: Anaemia is described in the blood-test interpretation.
note: The literal “without blood” is not the clinical definition.

definition: The physiological process that stops bleeding.
plain: The body limits and stops blood loss.
example: Haemostasis involves blood vessels, platelets and coagulation.

definition: Abnormality of lymph nodes, commonly enlargement.
plain: Lymph nodes are abnormal or enlarged.
example: The examination records cervical lymphadenopathy.

definition: Enlargement of the spleen.
plain: The spleen is larger than expected.
example: Splenomegaly names a finding rather than its cause.

definition: Reduced ability of the immune system to defend against infection.
plain: The immune system’s defences are reduced.
example: The history includes an immunodeficiency.

definition: A blood glucose concentration above the appropriate range.
plain: Blood glucose is higher than expected.
example: Hyperglycaemia is a laboratory finding described in the note.

definition: A blood glucose concentration below the appropriate range.
plain: Blood glucose is lower than expected.
example: The teaching example contrasts hypoglycaemia with hyperglycaemia.

definition: A state of insufficient thyroid hormone action, usually from reduced production.
plain: There is too little thyroid hormone activity.
example: Hypothyroidism appears in the endocrine history.

definition: Relating to hormones released into the circulation by glands or specialised cells.
plain: Hormones travel through the blood to act elsewhere.
example: The thyroid is an endocrine gland.

definition: Blood in the urine.
plain: Blood is present in urine.
example: The referral documents haematuria.
note: Compare with uraemia: the order of the parts changes the meaning.

definition: Surgical removal of all or part of a kidney.
plain: An operation removes a kidney or a portion of it.
example: The procedure is specified as a partial nephrectomy.

definition: The presence or formation of stones in a kidney.
plain: There are stones in the kidney.
example: Nephrolithiasis is the kidney-stone term in the report.

definition: Visual examination of the bladder and urethra using a scope.
plain: A clinician looks inside the bladder with a small scope.
example: Cystoscopy is listed as a urological procedure.
note: Cyst/o can also mean a cyst or sac; in this term it refers to the urinary bladder.

definition: Pain or discomfort during urination.
plain: Passing urine is painful or uncomfortable.
example: The history records dysuria as a symptom.

definition: A reduced volume of urine output.
plain: Less urine is being produced than expected.
example: Oliguria describes urine output, not painful urination.

definition: A clinical syndrome caused by accumulation of waste products in severe kidney dysfunction.
plain: Waste products build up because the kidneys are not working adequately.
example: The teaching note contrasts uraemia with haematuria.
note: The modern clinical syndrome is broader than an isolated raised blood urea result.

definition: Inflammation of the ear.
plain: Part of the ear is inflamed.
example: Otitis media specifies the middle ear.

definition: The medical specialty concerned with the eyes and vision.
plain: The specialty that looks after eye health.
example: The patient has an ophthalmology appointment.

definition: Discharge from the nose.
plain: A runny nose.
example: Rhinorrhoea is recorded in the symptom history.

definition: Inflammation of a testis.
plain: A testicle is inflamed.
example: Orchitis names inflammation of testicular tissue.

definition: Surgical removal of all or part of the prostate.
plain: An operation removes prostate tissue.
example: The surgical history specifies the type of prostatectomy.

definition: Surgical removal of the uterus.
plain: An operation to remove the womb.
example: A hysterectomy does not, by itself, imply removal of the ovaries.

definition: Surgical removal of a fallopian tube or tubes.
plain: An operation removes one or both fallopian tubes.
example: The procedure is described as a bilateral salpingectomy.

definition: Relating to the period before birth.
plain: Before a baby is born.
example: Prenatal care refers to care during pregnancy.

definition: Relating to the newborn period, usually the first 28 days after birth.
plain: Relating to the first weeks of a baby’s life.
example: Neonatal is a timing term, not a description of prematurity.

definition: A person who is pregnant for the first time.
plain: This is their first pregnancy.
example: The obstetric history records primigravida.
note: Gravidity counts pregnancies; parity concerns pregnancies reaching a defined gestational threshold.

definition: Difficulty initiating or maintaining sleep, or waking too early.
plain: Difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep.
example: The history describes insomnia in the patient’s own words.
note: A symptom term; a clinical disorder requires additional criteria.

definition: Reduced ability to experience interest or pleasure.
plain: Activities that usually feel enjoyable no longer do.
example: The assessment asks about anhedonia without assuming a diagnosis.

definition: The mental processes involved in knowing, thinking, learning and remembering.
plain: How a person thinks, understands and remembers.
example: The note describes changes in cognition using specific observations.

definition: Non-malignant; a benign tumour does not invade surrounding tissue or metastasise.
plain: A tumour is not cancerous.
example: The pathology report characterises the tumour as benign.
note: Benign does not mean harmless in every location or situation.

definition: Describing cancer with the ability to invade tissue and potentially spread.
plain: Cancerous, with the potential to invade or spread.
example: Malignant is used to describe the biological behaviour of a tumour.

definition: Spread of cancer from its original site to another part of the body.
plain: Cancer has spread to another location.
example: The report distinguishes a metastasis from a new primary tumour.
note: Metastases is the plural form.

definition: The presence of bacteria in the bloodstream.
plain: Bacteria are present in the blood.
example: Bacteraemia and sepsis are not interchangeable terms.
note: Sepsis concerns life-threatening organ dysfunction from a dysregulated response to infection; bacteria in blood alone do not define it.

definition: Life-threatening organ dysfunction caused by a dysregulated response to infection.
plain: The body’s response to infection causes dangerous organ dysfunction.
example: A teaching note separates the meaning of sepsis from bacteraemia.
note: Not synonymous with “blood poisoning” or a positive blood culture.

definition: An organism or agent capable of causing disease.
plain: A germ or other agent that can cause disease.
example: The laboratory identifies a pathogen.

definition: The process of creating images using X-rays.
plain: Taking an X-ray image.
example: Radiography is the process; a radiograph is an image produced.

definition: Imaging that represents sections or slices of the body.
plain: Making images of thin sections through the body.
example: Computed tomography is abbreviated CT.

definition: Imaging with high-frequency sound waves.
plain: Sound waves are used to create images inside the body.
example: Ultrasonography uses sound rather than ionising X-rays.

definition: The study of how the body absorbs, distributes, metabolises and eliminates a medicine.
plain: What the body does to a medicine.
example: The lesson uses pharmacokinetics to describe drug handling.

definition: The study of a medicine’s effects and how those effects occur.
plain: What a medicine does to the body.
example: Pharmacodynamics concerns effects rather than the handling of the drug.

definition: The fraction of a dose that reaches the systemic circulation unchanged.
plain: How much of a given dose reaches the bloodstream unchanged.
example: The pharmacology discussion compares bioavailability between routes of administration.

definition: An approach used alongside conventional medical care.
plain: An additional approach used together with conventional care.
example: The word complementary describes how an approach is used.
note: The label does not establish evidence of benefit, safety or suitability.

definition: An approach used in place of conventional medical care.
plain: An approach used instead of conventional care.
example: The word alternative describes replacement rather than addition.
note: The label does not establish effectiveness or safety.

definition: The occurrence of new cases in a population at risk over a specified period.
plain: How many new cases develop over time.
example: The study reports incidence over a defined follow-up period.
note: A rate and a cumulative incidence use different denominators; always read the study’s definition.

definition: The proportion of a population with a condition at a specified time or during a defined period.
plain: How common a condition is in a population.
example: The survey reports point prevalence on a specified date.
note: Prevalence includes existing cases; incidence concerns new cases.

definition: A defined group of people followed or studied over time.
plain: A group whose outcomes are studied over time.
example: The research follows a cohort of healthcare workers.

plain: Towards the front.
example: The sternum is anterior to the heart.

definition: Towards the back of the body in anatomical position.
plain: Towards the back.
example: The vertebral column is posterior to the heart.

plain: Closer to where a limb or structure begins.
example: The elbow is proximal to the wrist.

definition: Further from the point of attachment or origin.
plain: Further from where a limb or structure begins.

plain: Closer to the centre line.

definition: Away from the midline of the body.
plain: Further from the centre line.
